catalogue_requests.reason: cap.imaging.focus.v1 measures its search range and target position in um, while this microscope's autofocus takes a list of stage z positions in the stage's own unit (microscope.py:148-170) and the clone states no micrometre conversion (the upstream labels the axis 'position (Microsteps)', microscope.py:351); no class can express a scan in stage units without inventing a conversion

notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); the gate raised no warning. Model-authored and unreviewed: nothing ran on a microscope, and the R1 hardware backend opens the Pi camera and the stage only when an operator passes it with allow_hardware. MOCK PATH: the card prefers the upstream simulator, but the clone's only stand-in is DummyStage, which replaces the stage alone (microscope.py:281-291) while load_microscope(dummy_stage=True) still needs a real picamera camera, so the package ships a fake of the whole Microscope object instead (recorded commands, no images). NOT COVERED: the image array and everything that returns or stores it - rgb_image()/rgb_image_old() return a numpy array (microscope.py:111-131), acquire_image_stack() writes JPEG files into a caller-chosen directory (microscope.py:172-202), and the standard has no channel for an image artifact (no image capability is bound); freeze_camera_settings(), save_settings(), the lens shading calibration and the keyboard/characterisation tooling are also outside the package. The clone states no maximum zoom and no stage travel range, so the zoom write is bounded only at its documented 1.0 floor and the autofocus z positions are Limit.operator_required (site-limits.example.json is the template; every scan is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET until the site fills it). The native stop is close(), which shuts the camera and the stage down; there is no separate hardware e-stop claim (the card's floor is R1, and nothing here is safety-rated). check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-10-29; reviewed_by stays null): accepted after a reviewer edit: native.py no longer says that the loader refuses this R1 hardware backend (it refuses only R2 and above). After the registry rebuild refreshed task.json, the reviewer re-ran the gate and wrote its digest above.
